item.title: Supreme Court Again Blocks Republican-Backed Missouri Voting Map
item.description: The ruling deferred to the state’s Supreme Court, which had invalidated G.O.P.-friendly district lines, saying voters must first have an opportunity to approve the map in a statewide referendum.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow and Mitch Smith
item.media:credit: Yong Li Xuan/Missourian, via AP
item.media:description: A protest at the Missouri State Capitol last September over the proposed redistricting plan.

item.title: D.O.J. Escalates Threats to States in Battle for Election Records
item.description: The department sent letters to at least 30 states demanding they retain election records, an outgrowth of President Trump’s baseless claims of widespread election fraud.
item.dc:creator: Nick Corasaniti
item.media:credit: Mark Abramson for The New York Times
item.media:description: Workers at the Los Angeles County election center in November 2024. The Department of Justice sued about 30 states to force them to send unredacted voter lists in its efforts to find widespread fraud.

item.title: Trump Wants to Give Out $5,000 Checks. It Would Cost More Than $1 Trillion.
item.description: The president’s idea to hand every American adult a “dividend” if Republicans keep control of Congress likely would need congressional approval, exacerbate the deficit and lead to a rise in inflation, experts said.

item.title: Anthropic Says It Blocked Possible Efforts to Build Biological Weapons
item.description: In a new report, the A.I. start-up added that it could not determine if the research was legitimate or nefarious, leading the company to shut down the work.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Volz
item.media:credit: Marissa Leshnov for The New York Times
item.media:description: The report Anthropic published on Thursday cataloged a litany of misuses of its A.I. models, including the chatbot Claude, over the past eight months.

item.title: The Mathematician Crushed Between OpenAI and Anthropic Over a Math Problem
item.description: Tristan Buckmaster was on the path toward an important proof when one of the A.I. giants used its staggering resources to get there first.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chang
item.media:credit: Graham Dickie for The New York Times
item.media:description: Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematician at New York University, in front of a chalkboard where he marked a timeline of events leading up to OpenAI’s announcement, and his own research progress, on solving the Navier-Stokes equations.

item.title: A.I. Data Center Pollution Poses Health Threat, Former E.P.A. Officials Warn
item.description: Air pollution from gas-fired power plants to run data centers is expected to add at least $20 billion in annual health care costs by 2028, the group warns.
item.dc:creator: Hiroko Tabuchi

item.media:description: A neighborhood near the construction site of a Meta A.I. data center in El Paso, Texas.

item.title: After a Difficult Loss, Nigeria Has Become a Source of Pain for Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
item.description: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie has moved countless readers with her novels about Nigerians at home and abroad. After the death in Lagos of her toddler son, her homeland no longer feels as much like home.
item.dc:creator: Veronica Chambers

item.title: He Lost His Mother on 9/11. He Grew Up in Her Childhood Bedroom.
item.description: Jacob Campbell was a baby when his mother was killed, and he has struggled to come to terms with the tragedy that shaped him. For the grandmother who raised him, it’s even harder.
item.dc:creator: Katherine Rosman and Hiroko Masuike
item.media:description: Jacob Campbell, right, stands with his grandmother, Jeanne Maurer, in front of a tree he planted when he was a child in memory of his mother, Jill, who died on Sept. 11.

item.title: Trump’s Trade War With Canada Is Making Even Sprinkle Makers Nervous

item.title: Carney, at a Cabinet Retreat, Considers Further Trade Strikes Against the U.S.
item.description: Canada’s retaliation this week against President Trump’s tariffs was met with more American tariffs and a closed U.S. border on some Canadian products.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:credit: Chris Tanouye/Reuters
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada will consider whether to impose more tariffs against the United States during his cabinet retreat, which starts on Thursday.

item.title: Gander Welcomed Americans in 2001. Now, U.S.-Canada Tensions Hit Home.
item.description: The Newfoundland town welcomed thousands of frightened airline passengers on Sept. 11, but 25 years later, mixed emotions run through anniversary plans amid an escalating trade war.
item.dc:creator: Norimitsu Onishi and Renaud Philippe
item.media:credit: Renaud Philippe for The New York Times
item.media:description: A scene from the play Come From Away, performed in Gander, Newfoundland and Labrador. The musical tells the story of the 6,579 passengers and crew aboard 38 planes diverted to Gander after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks, and of the local residents who welcomed and cared for them.

item.media:description: Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University in Orem before he was shot last year.

item.title: What Would Charlie Kirk Do Today?

item.media:description: People arrive at a memorial at the Turning Point USA headquarters in Phoenix, Ariz., to pay their respects to Charlie Kirk last year.
